 This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 21.09.2016 Passed In Mvc
No.546/2015 On The File Of The Judge, Principal Court
Of Small Causes And Mact, Mysuru, Partly Allowing
The Claim Petition For Compensation And Seeking
Enhancement Of Compensation.
 This Appeal Coming On For Hearing This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.546/2015 on 21.09.2016, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal.

2. The petitioner contended that on 30-11-2014 at 8.45 a.m., while he was walking on the foot path at Maddur Town, the driver of the car bearing KL-14-Q-2152 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained fracture of both right and left leg and was shifted to Maddur Government Hospital and later, to Basappa Memorial Hospital, Mysuru, for treatment.
A case was registered by the concerned Police against the car driver for negligent driving.
The petitioner contended that the owner and insurer are liable to compensate the petitioner for the injuries suffered by him.

On issuance of notice, the respondent No.1-owner remained ex-parte and respondent No.2 contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable and the drier of the car had violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
4. The Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner and another witness were examined on behalf of petitioner as PWs.1 and 2 and Exs.P1 to P13 were marked.
The copy of the policy was marked as Ex.R1 on behalf of the respondents.

5. After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `5,19,179/- as compensation under different heads as below:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN `) Loss of future earnings 97,344/-
 Medical Expenses 3,41,835/-
 Pain, injuries and sufferings 30,000/-
 Future Medical Expenses 50,000/-
 TOTAL 5,19,179/-

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant/petitioner before this Court contending that the NC: 2023:KHC:20720 compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate, meager and abysmally low.
7. On issuance of notice, respondent No.2-Insurance company has appeared through its counsel and the notice to the respondent No.1 was dispensed with.
On admitting the appeal, secured the Tribunal records.

8. Heard the arguments by both the sides and perused the Tribunal records.
9.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the notional income considered by the Tribunal and the functional disability decided by the Tribunal are not proper and correct.

It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal has no correlation to the injuries suffered, period of inpatient treatment, the nature and avocation of the petitioner and the impact of the injuries on his avocation.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company contend that the compensation awarded by NC: 2023:KHC:20720 the Tribunal is just, proper and correct and no enhancement is warranted.
11. The records reveal that the petitioner had suffered fracture of both the legs and he was treated with ORIF.
It is relevant to note that PW.2 who has assessed the disability stated that each of the lower limb have 12% disability.
The petitioner though claimed that he was Head Cook cum contractor and was earning `15,000/- per month, no evidence to prove the same were adduced by him.

Therefore, the Tribunal took notional income of the petitioner at `6,000/- per month, added 'future prospects' for the same and awarded the compensation holding the disability at 8%.
12.
In the absence of any cogent evidence to prove the income of the petitioner, the notional income has to be considered by the Tribunal.
The guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of disputes before the Lok-Adalat, prescribe the notional income of `8,500/- per month for the year 2014.

In umpteen number of decisions, this Court has held that such guidelines issued by the KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under NC:
2023:KHC:20720 the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income has to be considered at `8,500/- per month.
13. Coming to the disability and the avocation of the petitioner, he claims that he was a Head Cook but no document is available on record.
He was aged 50 years and there is no reason to discard his contention that he was a Head Cook.
He had suffered fracture of the bones of both the legs and PW.2 opined that physical disability together is 24%.
Such disability, when considered together with the avocation of the petitioner, would not be higher than the 1/3rd.
Hence, the disability of 8% is proper.
Adding the 'future prospects' by the Tribunal to the income of the petitioner appears to be incorrect.

Therefore, by applying the multiplier of '13', the 'loss of future earnings' is calculated at Sri. K. Chandre Gowda @ Chandru @ Raju vs Sri. Abdul Azeez on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98518712/

sentences.text: 14. Consequentially, the 'loss of income during laid up period' is enhanced to `25,500/- (`8500/- x 3).

15. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `3,41,835/- and `50,000/- towards the 'medical expenses'
and 'future medical expenses', which do not require any enhancement.
The compensation under he head of 'pain and suffering' at `30,000/- is inadequate and therefore, a sum of `40,000/- is awarded under this head.
17. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head of 'loss of amenities in life' and 'conveyance and nourishment and attendant charges'.

Therefore, a sum of `20,000/- and `10,000/-
is awarded to the petitioner under these heads.

Hence, the compensation is reassessed under different heads as below:

sentences.text: (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of `74,236/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
(iii) The respondent No.2- Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) Rest of the order of the Tribunal stands unaltered.
